title: Restore immutable event compatibility
objective: Fence the trusted validator to exact audited first-write provenance for known malformed immutable events without rewriting historical bytes, while keeping all newly emitted events strict and preserving byte-for-byte transition immutability.
acceptance: known malformed historical events are admitted only at exact audited relative paths with exact audited first-write Git blob identities
strict-valid normalization, byte mutation, path move, cloned historical eventId, duplicate eventId, and fresh backdated legacy events fail closed
the exact audited WorldEntity and MaterialDNA first-write bytes remain representable without mutation
all unlisted events remain subject to the strict V2 schema and malformed affects do not generalize beyond exact audited first-write bytes
transition-check rejects every historical event rewrite or deletion byte-for-byte and additionally rejects eventId replay on newly added events
deterministic/adversarial control tests and canonical CI pass on the exact reviewed head
integration sequencing accounts explicitly for already-laundered live Authority, WorldEntity, and cart bytes rather than treating compatibility as a trust reset
notes: Exact head 772416839f4e9a3330c89dc9880e1670b7191824 addresses every prior P0: historical exceptions are checked before strict validation; exact path plus first-write Git blob identity is required; strict-valid laundering and duplicate/replayed IDs are rejected; and the temporary restoration loophole was removed so byte immutability is unchanged. Canonical CI 31475546478 PASS; Swarm engine-tests 93728287438 PASS. Current live Authority/WorldEntity/cart bytes are already laundered, so this patch intentionally detects them as non-canonical. That pre-existing trust-continuity problem is a separate recovery dependency and must not be hidden inside compatibility. Independent exact-head rereview required.
